assumptions.summary: Person suspiciousness depends on both contacts and topics.
Message influence is bidirectional, so sender and receiver are treated symmetrically.
Known labels stay fixed at 1 or 0 while ordinary people start at 0.5.
One multi-topic message is split into single-topic messages.
Different contacts impose independent suspiciousness impacts.
Influence decays exponentially with network distance or iteration.
Topic R is the rate at which suspiciousness is transmitted by a topic.
The top 20 in the priority list are treated as probable conspirators for follow-up counts.
In the virus analogy, an individual's transmission ability is constant.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The Summary states a communication network and person/topic quantities whose final S ranking produces a priority list.
Table 1 defines 83 people, 910 preprocessed messages, 15 topics, S/R, and decay degrees.
Two self-messages and one invalid topic-18 row are deleted; duplicate names receive suffixes; multi-topic records are split.
Each message edge is duplicated with sender and receiver swapped to enforce bidirectional influence.
The basic case fixes eight known conspirators, eight known non-conspirators, and three suspicious topics.
Manager evidence separates marked, conspiratorial, and total message counts.
Chris and topic 1 introduce a local information-update graph with concrete interlocutor and edge tables.
Topic-specific initial R values are assigned from textual characteristics and described as casual deduction.
The proposed semantic pipeline uses topic extraction, attitude/emotion analysis, and interactive relations.
The transfer example maps S to virion level and R_ij*S_i to expected infectious-particle transmission.

dependency_graph.handoff: The two-phase scores expose chain saturation, so prior/current exponential blending is introduced.
Person and topic rankings are handed to contextual manager checks and leader-contact counts.
The priority workflow is rerun after new person/topic information and parameter changes.
The observed topic abstraction failure motivates semantic refinement and qualified transfer.
Future text or target-domain features would require a fresh source-checked two-phase rerun.

language_observations.summary: Human style is carried by concrete repair, failure-triggered decay, score qualification, recomputation, parameter honesty, semantic repair, and qualified transfer.
summary moves from task to two-phase method: Name the network task, assign person/topic quantities, alternate two update phases, and end with a ranked output plus evaluation boundary.

behavioral intuition becomes a bidirectional assumption: Use an everyday communication example to justify a typed graph direction or contact premise, then expose the preprocessing needed to make the data conform.
a concrete data anomaly triggers local expurgation: State the bad row or identity conflict, give the reason for expurgation or renaming, and preserve the downstream denominator change.
an intuition is turned into paired functions: Move from message and topic intuition to explicit person and topic functions, then hand both to an alternating iterative process.
an algorithm hands off between person and topic phases: Make update order visible: initialize, propagate person, propagate topic, decay, repeat, and return the person ranking.
a circular union is handed to recursive calculation: Define neighbor impact, combine independent contacts with a probabilistic union, and reduce the calculation recursively until a one-neighbor case.
a chain saturation failure triggers exponential decay: Show that repeated propagation drives every unknown toward one, then retain prior values with a shrinking current-update weight.
a table reading directs the next investigation: Read a ranked score table, compare a topic or subgroup, and turn the numeric pattern into a bounded follow-up rather than a verdict.

high scores are downgraded without corroborating messages: Separate a high network score from message-context evidence and explain why a broad-contact manager can look suspicious without being confirmed.
contact counts yield leader candidates: Choose a candidate population, count suspicious contacts, rank the counts, and call the names probable leaders with the boundary visible.

a topic abstraction error motivates semantic repair: Give a named case where coarse topic membership misleads the ranking, then propose message-content, attitude, or relation extraction to recover the distinction.
new person/topic information causes local recomputation: Add a person and topic link, rerun the model, point to rank changes near the new evidence, and explain why distant nodes move less.

casual priors are admitted and tested by sensitivity: Declare topic-specific starting values as a casual deduction, compare the revised priority list, and use the shift to bound confidence in initialization.
parameter ablations expose the propagation mechanism: Set decay rates to extreme values, observe saturation or fixed-topic behavior, and connect the result to the role of the parameter.

a shared propagation mechanism motivates qualified transfer: Map node state and edge transmission to a new domain, state an omitted dynamic, and qualify the result as an estimate for a matching network property.

The final S list highlights people and topic values, then directs attention to a Spanish-word topic clue.

Topic and semantic refinements are proposed to reduce misclassification.
The virus network is a qualified mechanism analogy and the final drawback records one-sided score accumulation.

title: Crime Busting by An Iterative 2-phase Propagation Method
unresolved_questions: The paper deletes self-messages and an invalid topic-18 row and renames duplicate people, but provides no versioned correction log or sensitivity audit for the changed denominator.
Duplicated sender/receiver edges are created to enforce bidirectional influence, so the graph direction is altered before inference and is not independently tested.
Known conspirators and non-conspirators are fixed at 1 and 0 while ordinary people start at 0.5; label certainty and initialization leakage are not audited.
The independence assumption behind the union formula is asserted as a local convenience and is not checked against correlated contacts or repeated messages.
The recursive union and the displayed Cji notation do not specify repeated-neighbor handling, message direction, or how a zero or empty neighborhood is treated.
Equation 3 can have a zero denominator and inherits the circular person-score interpretation; no domain restriction, clipping rule, or uncertainty is given.
A chain with one known conspirator drives every Si toward 1, motivating decay but also showing that graph reachability alone can overwhelm benign context.
DRS=DRR=0.5 and the stopping/convergence language are hand-set; no tolerance, contraction proof, or initialization stability metric is reported.
Table 3's topic clue and Spanish-word explanation are internal readings, not an independently labeled language or conspiracy finding.
The five-manager comparison is a useful contextual check but reuses priority-ranked people and gives no predeclared message-ratio threshold.
The top-20 candidate set is selected from the same priority list used to count contacts, so leader evidence is label- and selection-dependent.
Contact counts support probable leaders but do not measure control, brokerage, direction, or causal leadership.
The coarse topic example can reverse a person's interpretation, but the proposed NLP correction has no corpus, annotation, or held-out test.
Latent Dirichlet Allocation and probabilistic latent semantic indexing are named as future improvements without a reproducible extraction pipeline.
Topic-specific R values are admitted to come from casual deduction and are not calibrated or elicited with uncertainty.
The Chris/topic-1 graph visually explains local rank movement, but figure edge semantics, time, and direction are not frozen.
The claim that distant nodes change less is a same-network sensitivity observation, not independent stability validation.
Rank jumps of p32 and other nodes are interpreted through Table 7/8 while the appendix comparison is not a held-out evaluation.
The DRS=DRR=1 ablation produces widespread scores near one, demonstrating saturation but not selecting a valid decay rate.
The DRR=0 ablation freezes topic suspicion, but the change in person ranks is not compared with an external topic label or loss.
The scalability claim has no runtime, memory, sampling, privacy, or deployment evidence.
The virus application ignores within-person growth and maps S/R to infection transmission without biomedical labels, intervention costs, ethics, or target validation.
The source states that a low-S neighbor can only increase suspicion, so benign contacts cannot lower a score and accumulated weak ties can create false positives.
Appendix Table 13, Contents, headers, formula-only blocks, chart labels, citations, and cited wording are excluded from positive language evidence; the official task statement is unavailable.

writing_logic.summary: network task -> person/topic quantities -> Person/Topic phases -> decay -> priority list -> sensitivity and transfer
given known/unknown people -> priority-list output -> mutually affecting person/topic suspicion -> two-phase propagation
bidirectional behavior -> graph preprocessing -> swapped edges and split topics -> 910-message denominator
intuition -> S/R definitions -> iterative algorithm -> formula and phase handoff
chain saturation -> exponential decay -> prior/current blend -> convergence boundary
rank and topic table -> Spanish-word clue -> bounded investigation direction
high score -> manager message context -> ratio comparison -> probable but qualified conclusion
top-20 candidate set -> suspicious-contact count -> probable leader candidates
coarse topic membership -> Harry/Dave/George misreading -> message content and NLP repair
new Chris/topic-1 evidence -> local graph -> p32 rank jump -> distant-node comparison
casual topic priors -> new R initialization -> changed priority list -> sensitivity admission
DRS/DRR controls -> extreme settings -> saturation or fixed-topic output -> mechanism reading
shared propagation property -> virus network mapping -> omitted within-person growth -> qualified transfer
low-S neighbor -> one-sided increase -> accumulated weak ties -> model drawback
